extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, and regulated parties tracking Department of Homeland Security proposed rules (especially maritime operators, event organizers, immigration practitioners, and industry affected by DHS regulatory changes)
extracted.subtask_description: An aggregated listing of Department of Homeland Security proposed rules (Federal Register API results) with short abstracts describing the rule's purpose, regulatory change, and invitations for public comment. Covers Coast Guard maritime regulations, fee adjustments, bond transmission, cyber-incident reporting, and immigration-related rule proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Local Regulation (SLR) purpose and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: SLR established to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards inherent in recurring or single marine events; non-participating persons and vessels would be prohibited from being in the regulated area unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port (COTP) or designated representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for boat races, raft races, paddle events, swim events, and other marine events; may modify starting point location or other specifics. SLRs can be temporary or recurring; regulated area coordinates and precise boundaries are specified in the rule. The rule text typically 'invites your comments on this proposed rulemaking.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety zone purpose and prohibition rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Safety zones are proposed to protect personnel, vessels, and the marine environment from potential hazards created by specified events (e.g., fireworks displays, swimmers under bridges, marine events); the proposed rulemaking would prohibit persons and vessels from being in the safety zone unless specifically authorized by the Captain of the Port, Sector or designated representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety zones may be temporary for single events or updated in tables of recurring events; proposals may correct coordinates or amend dates. Enforcement mechanism: authorization by COTP; typical justification focuses on public safety and navigable water protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security zone for high-profile events
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary security zones may be established for navigable waters in connection with high-profile events (e.g., FIFA World Cup and Fan Fest) to safeguard official parties, VIPs, and other participants because waterfront access presents security concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities such as anchoring or remaining within the security zone are prohibited unless authorized by the Captain of the Port or designated representative; justification emphasizes security for attendees and VIP protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee adjustment to recover costs
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS proposes adjusting user fees (example: increase fee for adjudicating Form I-246 from $155 to $755) to recover the costs of providing the service when fees have not been adjusted for decades.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee adjustments are presented with cost-recovery rationale and technical edits to the regulation; they follow agency cost accounting and notice procedures in the NPRM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic bond transmission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to require most bonds collected by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to be transmitted electronically to CBP via a specialized system by the surety or by the principal on a cash-secured bond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to centralize and streamline CBP's bond program; changes affect how bonds are submitted and who must transmit them (surety or principal), with implementation details specified in regulation amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment authorization eligibility and processing criteria for asylum applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed changes to regulations governing asylum applications and employment authorization based on a pending asylum application, including pausing acceptance of EAD applications during periods when affirmative asylum average processing time exceeds 180 days, extending the waiting period to apply for employment authorization to 365 days, changing EAD application processing time requirements, and adding eligibility requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule frames eligibility, filing timing, and processing requirements intended to manage workload and program integrity; proposals typically describe operational thresholds (e.g., 180-day trigger) and process changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing shipping safety fairways and vessel routing measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals to establish shipping safety fairways and related vessel routing measures along specified coastlines to preserve safe and reliable transit of vessels along well-established traffic patterns and further improve navigation safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often accompanied by programmatic environmental review (e.g., draft Programmatic Environmental Impact Statement) and extended comment periods; rulemaking justifies routing by safety and traffic-pattern preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CIRCIA implementation stakeholder input and scope/burden refinement
rubrics_metrics.description: Town hall meetings and notices intended to allow external stakeholders opportunity to provide input on refining the scope and burden of the Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act (CIRCIA) Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, which seeks to implement covered cyber incident and ransom payment reporting requirements for covered entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency solicits stakeholder information to inform definition of covered entities, reporting thresholds, and burden estimates; procedural accommodation (town halls, reopened comment periods) is used to refine NPRM scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairway anchorages establishment rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishment of new fairway anchorages in deeper water to accommodate vessels with deeper drafts (e.g., petroleum tankers), intended to enhance navigation safety, efficient transportation of energy resources, economic growth, and national energy security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule rationale ties placement and depth of anchorages to operational needs of maritime commerce and safety; agency describes expected benefits to commerce and navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction and amendment of regulatory tables and coordinates
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments may correct inaccurate coordinates, edit event names, add or remove safety zones, or add dates to recurring events listings to ensure regulatory tables accurately reflect current conditions or jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical corrections are issued to maintain accuracy of geographic and temporal regulatory data; changes are often limited to administrative/coordinate fixes but are published as NPRMs when they amend CFR entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between temporary and recurring regulatory actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules distinguish temporary actions (single-event safety zones or SLRs for a specific date/event) from recurring SLRs and safety zones (annual events or ongoing special local regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary actions specify dates and are time-limited; recurring regulations are added to tables and may have ongoing applicability and require different administrative descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation for public comment on proposed rulemakings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nearly all listed proposed rules end with an invitation: 'We invite your comments on this proposed rulemaking.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invitations signal the notice-and-comment process under the Administrative Procedure Act; rules often provide instructions for submitting comments, deadlines, and sometimes reopen or extend comment periods when coupled with related environmental documents.
